summary: Age of Empires entries from the prepared 1000-title candidate queue, researched for Sami's fidelity-first archive route.

entries.title: Age of Empires II: The Age of Kings
entries.definitive_edition: Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition

emulation.notes: Use the current native or official release route where available.

primary.version: Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition
primary.why: Definitive Edition is the best fidelity/completeness route, with original campaigns and expansions presented with improved modern presentation; the original release family spans Windows, Mac, and PS2.
primary.how_to_play: Play Definitive Edition on Windows with the current patch. Use the base DE content for The Age of Kings campaigns, then add expansion/DLC campaigns only when archiving the broader Age II lineage.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Ensemble Studios release family; historically authoritative but lower resolution and missing later expansion/remaster quality-of-life work.
all_releases.reason: skip: preserved by DE for normal play unless comparing original AI/UI behavior.

all_releases.fidelity: Console conversion of the original RTS.
all_releases.reason: skip: lower input/fidelity route and no sourced exclusive campaign content needed for Sami's archive.

all_releases.platform: Age of Empires II: HD Edition on Windows
all_releases.fidelity: Earlier PC remaster route superseded for normal archive use by Definitive Edition.
all_releases.reason: skip: DE has the stronger current fidelity/completeness case.

all_releases.platform: Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition on Windows / Xbox / PlayStation / macOS
all_releases.fidelity: Modern remaster with improved visuals and original campaigns/expansions; Windows remains best for RTS input and capture.
all_releases.reason: primary: best modern route for fidelity plus campaign completeness.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced exclusive-content split requires a secondary route for this archive entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: Definitive Edition includes and extends beyond the 1999 base game; log which campaigns/DLC are being archived so The Age of Kings itself stays distinct from later expansion content.

entries.title: Age of Empires

emulation.notes: Native Windows Definitive Edition is the archive primary.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows PC Definitive Edition at modern resolution

primary.why: Definitive Edition is the best fidelity/completeness route for the 1997 game: the modernized release has 4K visuals, as a remaster of Age of Empires plus The Rise of Rome. The original Windows/Mac releases are preserved for historical comparison, not the main archive run.
primary.how_to_play: Play Age of Empires: Definitive Edition on Windows through Steam or the Microsoft/Xbox PC ecosystem with the current patch. Use the original Windows or Mac version only when comparing original Genie-engine behavior, UI, or balance.

all_releases.fidelity: Original 2D RTS release with the historical UI and balance but lower modern display and compatibility ceiling.
all_releases.reason: skip: historically important, but Definitive Edition is the stronger complete play route for normal archive capture.

all_releases.fidelity: Mac port of the original release family.
all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced exclusive campaign content over the PC/Definitive route.

all_releases.fidelity: Handheld conversion route with a much lower practical archive ceiling.
all_releases.reason: skip: platform curiosity only; no sourced exclusive campaign content over the definitive PC route.

all_releases.platform: Age of Empires: The Rise of Rome / Gold Edition on Windows
all_releases.fidelity: Expansion and bundled original-era content route.
all_releases.reason: skip: the expansion content is covered by Definitive Edition for the main route; use only for original-release comparison.

all_releases.platform: Age of Empires: Definitive Edition on Windows
all_releases.fidelity: Modernized PC release with 4K visual presentation and current PC capture/settings ceiling.
all_releases.reason: primary: best fidelity plus included Rise of Rome content in a maintained PC package.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Definitive Edition resolves the normal fidelity/completeness route by bundling the original game and Rise of Rome content in the current PC remaster path.

entries.remaster_caveats: Use original Windows/Mac only for historical behavior comparison. Return of Rome content inside Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition is related series content, not the main Age of Empires 1997 archive route.

entries.title: Age of Empires IV
entries.definitive_edition: Current Windows PC Anniversary Edition/build with expansion state documented

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Current PC build with keyboard/mouse controls

primary.why: Age of Empires IV is a modern live-patched RTS, and the PC version remains the best route for keyboard/mouse control, capture, ranked/custom play, mods, and expansions. Console and PlayStation ports are valid access routes but not the control/capture baseline.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current PC build through Steam/Microsoft Store/Game Pass. Record build/date, owned expansions, civilizations available, campaign/skirmish/ranked scope, mods, input method, graphics settings, and online-service state.

secondary.what_to_play: Use only if documenting console RTS controls.
secondary.why: PC is the baseline for AoE IV control and capture.

all_releases.fidelity: Original and current RTS route, with PC preferred for controls/capture.

all_releases.platform: Xbox One / Xbox Series X|S / PlayStation 5

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Patch/build, expansion ownership, civ roster, mods, and online service state define the current route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record build, expansions, civs, campaign/ranked scope, mods, and online state.

entries.title: Age of Empires Online
entries.definitive_edition: Project Celeste current community-server route, labeled as post-shutdown restoration

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Project Celeste client with exact account/civilization/content state documented

primary.version: Project Celeste community server route after official shutdown
primary.why: The official Age of Empires Online service shut down in 2014, so current play requires the Project Celeste fan/community server. That route restores and expands content, so archive notes must label it separately from the official Microsoft live-service state.
primary.how_to_play: Use Project Celeste if documenting current play. Record launcher/client version, account/server, civilization, quest/gear/capital city state, PvE/PvP mode, added community content, and the official shutdown context.

secondary.platform: Original Microsoft/Games for Windows Live service

all_releases.fidelity: Official live-service route, shut down in 2014.
Current fan/community server route with restored and added content.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Project Celeste restores and expands the game but is not the official 2011-2014 service state.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record official shutdown and any Project Celeste-added civilizations/quests/content.
